through the chair. This report addresses a combination of structural challenges and a projected
depletion of the city's special events reserve beginning in 2026. Demand for the special event funding
has rebounded strongly post-pandemic, while annual contributions to the reserve were reduced in
recent years to support tax stability. Combined with existing commitments to major headline events
and a prior one time transfer from the reserve in 2023, the reserve is no longer able to support a continued
practice of awarding all eligible applicants up to the maximum allowable funding level. For 2026,
the reserve has approximately $133,900 available in uncommitted funds. While grant requests received
in 2026 already exceed $655,000 with additional intake periods remaining. Without action, the reserve
will be fully depleted and the traditional intake method would introduce inequities in access to funding for
events. The report outlines three options to address this issue for 26 and 27. Option one, which is
administration's recommendation, support special event funding and creates capacity and the reserve
to support headline events through a one-time transfer from the civic hospitality reserve and a
return of funds transferred to the fiscal stabilization reserve in 2023. Option two relies solely on a
transfer from the civic hospitality reserve and can support special event funding, but does not create
any capacity for funding headline events. Option three limits funding to existing reserve levels
and creates a significant gap between existing application anticipated special event grant funding
and the level of funding the reserve can support. Regardless of the option chosen, administration is also
recommending temporary program changes to increase fairness, transparency, and fiscal responsibility. These
include halting additional intakes for 2026 and adjudicating the existing applications as one intake.
The administration also proposes moving to a single annual intake in 2027, which would be held in the
fall of 2026. The available funds, as outlined in the report options for both 26 and 27,
would be applied collectively to that years intake of applications and a fixed percentage of support
across all eligible applications would be calculated as outlined in the report. The administration
would also commit to reporting back prior to the 2029 business and budget plan deliberations with
recommendations for policy and funding adjustments to support the special events reserved into the
future. Administration recommends option one because it offers the strongest short-term stability
allows the city to better satisfy existing 2026 commitments. It aligns with the 2027 budget to prove
by council, it avoids additional mill rate impact, and it also provides time to develop long-term
solutions ahead of the 2029 budget cycle. With that, administration is happy to answer questions.
